notes: The catalogue's arduino-due card lacks digital pins 2 and 3 and A0, which this tutorial needs. I defined one new part type, arduino-due-r3, with the full Due header pinout, and due1 uses it. The 3.3 V pin is named '3.3V', the same as the other catalogue boards (Uno, Mega).

E8 voltage warning: not a real problem for this manual, so the circuit is unchanged. The Due's 6-20 V requirement applies to its VIN or power-jack input. Here the 3.3V pin is an output feeding the breadboard rail, not a supply input. The board itself is powered over its USB cable, which the tutorial does not list or draw, so I did not add one.
The only voltage on the breadboard is 3.3V from the Due's own regulator, so the Due's 3.3 V-only inputs are never driven from 5 V.
The tutorial lists exactly 1 Due, 1 breadboard, 1 10k potentiometer, 2 push buttons, 2 10k resistors and jumper wires. The 11 jumper wires are counted from the circuit image.

The breadboard column numbers and rail hole numbers are my own layout choice, because the image does not give exact holes. Each button's side 1 goes to 3.3V. Side 2 carries the Due pin wire and the 10k pull-down resistor to ground, as the text says.

The potentiometer's outer legs go to 3.3V and ground, and its wiper (SIG) goes to A0 through the yellow wire. DAC0 and DAC1 are left unconnected, because the tutorial only says to probe them with an optional oscilloscope.
